Answer: B
Reason: The chest X-ray shows marked asymmetry with a smaller, hyperlucent right hemithorax and diminished vascular markings, while the CT confirms calcification and narrowing of the right pulmonary artery. These findings are characteristic of Takayasu arteritis causing chronic obstruction of the right pulmonary artery, leading to oligemia (Westermark sign) rather than acute embolism, effusion, or consolidation.
